# What PyPI API tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# A token is the prefix pypi- and, behind it, a macaroon serialized into
# base64url. The three characters the serialization opens with are the same in
# every token — a version number, the field number of a location, and the top
# two bits of that location's length — so pypi-AgE is what a token is located
# by, and what stands after those three is the location itself: pypi.org
# encodes to AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc and test.pypi.org to AgENdGVzdC5weXBpLm9yZw.
#
# Every token below is written that way and then finished with the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdef, which no real credential is. What the run stands in for is
# the identifier, the caveats and the signature, which a real token carries a
# hundred and fifty or so characters of; the pattern reads them as a run rather
# than to a count, so forty-eight characters state the same grammar and leave a
# case that fits on a line.
#
# The two cases under the over-match heading carry no ordered run at all. They
# are not tokens and nobody issued them: what they hold is a blob that opens the
# way a token does, which is the whole of what the pattern asks for.

patterns: pypi-api-token

# The indexes. What tells a token apart is the serialization, not the index that
# issued it, so a token from test.pypi.org is located beside one from pypi.org
# and so is one from an index nobody has named — the third case is a location of
# x.io. Both rulesets that read this format read pypi.org into their
# expressions and locate nothing in the second or the third.

case: a token from pypi.org in an environment assignment
in:   PYPI_API_TOKEN=pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  PYPI_API_TOKEN=«pypi-api-token»

case: a token from test.pypi.org
in:   pypi-AgENdGVzdC5weXBpLm9yZw0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «pypi-api-token»

case: a token from an index this pattern was never told about
in:   pypi-AgEEeC5pbw0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «pypi-api-token»

# The places a token is written. The username PyPI asks for beside it,
# __token__, is not a credential and stays in the text.

case: a token in the password field of a pypirc
in:   [pypi]\n  username = __token__\n  password = pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  [pypi]\n  username = __token__\n  password = «pypi-api-token»

case: a token on a twine command line
in:   twine upload -u __token__ -p pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef dist/*
out:  twine upload -u __token__ -p «pypi-api-token» dist/*

case: a token in a workflow secret
in:   {"secrets":{"PYPI_API_TOKEN":"pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}}
out:  {"secrets":{"PYPI_API_TOKEN":"«pypi-api-token»"}}

# The alphabet the body is written in. It is base64url with the padding
# stripped, which is what pymacaroons writes: the letters of both cases, the
# digits, the hyphen and the underscore. The two characters standard base64
# writes in place of the last two, the plus and the slash, are not admitted —
# and because the body is read to the end of its run, a character outside the
# alphabet standing inside a token leaves what is in front of it short of the
# floor rather than leaving a shorter token.

case: a body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef-0123456789abcdef_0123456789abcdef
out:  «pypi-api-token»

case: a plus inside the body
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef+0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef+0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a slash inside the body
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a dot inside the body
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef.0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# How long a body is, which the pattern reads as a floor and not as a count.
# What a macaroon carries between its location and its signature is a caveat
# list, and what stands in it differs by how the token was issued: projects,
# a user, or a Trusted Publisher and an expiry. So a count is what this scan is
# written not to read. The floor is fifty characters, the
# base64url length of the smallest macaroon that can be written at all, and the
# two cases below stand at it and one character short of it. What the lower one
# costs is on the record: a token cut short of the floor comes through, and what
# is left in the text is a version byte, a field number and the opening of a
# domain name rather than the signature a macaroon is a credential by.

case: a body exactly as long as the floor
in:   pypi-AgE0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:  «pypi-api-token»

case: a body one character short of the floor
in:   pypi-AgE0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd
out:  pypi-AgE0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcd

# What a token may be written against, and what it draws in. The anchor is the
# whole of what a token is found by and there is no boundary on either side of
# it, so a token keeps its span whatever word character stands in front of it.
# Behind it the redaction reaches to the end of the run, which is the price of
# reading a run rather than a count: a character of the token's own alphabet
# written straight after a token is redacted with the token, and a space, a dot
# or a quote is not.

case: a token after an underscore
in:   PYPI_API_TOKEN_pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  PYPI_API_TOKEN_«pypi-api-token»

case: a token after a letter
in:   xpypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  x«pypi-api-token»

case: a token at the end of a sentence
in:   the token is pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:  the token is «pypi-api-token».

case: a token inside quotes
in:   export PYPI_API_TOKEN="pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
out:  export PYPI_API_TOKEN="«pypi-api-token»"

case: a token before a hyphenated word
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:  «pypi-api-token»

case: a token before a word
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:  «pypi-api-token»

# Two tokens written together. Every character of the anchor belongs to the
# alphabet a body is, so a token can begin inside the span of the one before it;
# the two spans overlap and are redacted as one. Written apart, both go.

case: a token beginning inside the token before it
in:   pypi-AgEpypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «pypi-api-token»

case: two tokens separated by a space
in:   pypi-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef pypi-AgENdGVzdC5weXBpLm9yZw0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  «pypi-api-token» «pypi-api-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The anchor is eight characters
# of the base64url alphabet, so a long enough encoding written in that alphabet
# carries them somewhere, and everything from there to the end of the encoding
# is redacted. That is the answer rather than a fault in it: what is taken is a
# stretch of a value already opaque to a reader, and the tightening on offer is
# the location — reading pypi.org into the anchor, which is what both published
# rulesets do and what leaves a TestPyPI token in the output whole. A stale
# reading costs a credential and this costs a reader nothing. The pattern's own
# file weighs both.

case: the anchor inside a longer run of the alphabet
in:   payload=zzzzpypi-AgEzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
out:  payload=zzzz«pypi-api-token»

case: the anchor where a signature stands
in:   eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzpypi-AgEzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
out:  eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«pypi-api-token»

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first three are the three characters
# of the header: read in the case the serialization writes them, read in all
# three, and asked for at all. The fourth is the one shape of header the pattern
# declines on purpose — AgF is what a location of sixty-four characters or more
# encodes to, which is a domain name no index has, and the case is here so that
# the assumption is on the record. The three after them are the prefix, read in
# its own case, in all five of its characters, and asked for against the header
# rather than apart from it. The one after those turns the pair around and
# writes the header with no prefix in front of it at all, so that neither half
# is read as a token on its own. Of the last three, the names carrying pypi- are
# what a line about the index is full of and the header is the whole of what
# turns them away; a digest carries no hyphen for the prefix and neither a g nor
# an E for the header; and no word of prose is spelled with either.

case: a header in the wrong case
in:   pypi-age0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:  pypi-age0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case: two characters of the header
in:   pypi-Ag0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-Ag0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a body carrying no header at all
in:   pypi-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a header spelling a location of sixty-four characters or more
in:   pypi-AgFA0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-AgFA0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: an uppercase prefix
in:   PyPI-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  PyPI-AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: an underscore where the prefix carries a hyphen
in:   pypi_AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi_AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a dot between the prefix and the header
in:   pypi-.AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  pypi-.AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: the header with no prefix in front of it
in:   AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:  AgEIcHlwaS5vcmc0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case: a line of names carrying the prefix
in:   the gh-action-pypi-publish workflow replaced pypi-timemachine and pypi-server
out:  the gh-action-pypi-publish workflow replaced pypi-timemachine and pypi-server

case: a hexadecimal digest
in:   sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:  sha1=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case: prose
in:   there is no credential in this sentence
out:  there is no credential in this sentence

# And a PyPI credential this pattern has nothing to say about. A project's
# Trusted Publisher exchange hands back a token of exactly this shape, so that
# one is redacted; what is not is the OpenID Connect token a workflow sends to
# get it, which is a JWT and is the JWT pattern's to locate — with that pattern
# out of the set, the string comes through whole.

case: an openid connect token offered in exchange for one
in:   {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef"}
out:  {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.0123456789abcdef"}
